exposure: maternal coagulation function indicators (Platelet count, thrombin time, fibrinogen, prothrombin time, activated partial thromboplastin time, international normalized ratio) measured at 28-34 weeks of gestation
outcome: occurrence, progression, and severity of hypertensive disorders in pregnancy (HDP)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 300 pregnant women from Jinan Maternity and Child Care Hospital between October 2020 and October 2023, comprising 182 women diagnosed with hypertensive disorders in pregnancy (HDP) and 118 healthy pregnant women.
finding: Platelet count, thrombin time, and fibrinogen were identified as independent prognostic factors for pregnant women with HDP, and several coagulation indicators (PT, APTT, TT, Fib, INR) can reflect the severity of HDP.
mod_finding: Women with hypertensive disorders in pregnancy had a higher incidence of both vaginal delivery and cesarean section.
